resources.string: This app watches your concentration and holds notifications while you are focused. Android needs you to grant a few things first — the two marked Required are what actually hold notifications back.
You can continue without these, but notifications will be delivered normally until they are granted.
All set. You can change any of this later in Settings.
So the app can show its own ongoing notification while running, and deliver the catch-up summary when your focus breaks.
The Muse headband connects over Bluetooth. Without this the app has no signal to work from.
On this version of Android, Bluetooth scanning is gated behind location permission. The app does not use your location.
So the app knows what arrived while you were focused and can summarise it afterwards. It only records what arrived — it never reads message contents.
Android opens a list of every app on your phone. Find \"%1$s\" in it, turn it on, then come back here.
This is how notifications are actually held back. The app turns Do Not Disturb on while you are concentrating and off again when you stop.
Android opens its Do Not Disturb access list. Find \"%1$s\", allow it, then come back here.
Android and some phone manufacturers shut down background apps aggressively. Without this exemption the headset connection will be killed mid-session.
Running — deferral is active while you are focused
Standard deviations from your rolling baseline. The shaded band is the zone where nothing changes.
Waiting for the headset to settle…
Move the headband down onto your forehead and tuck the ear pieces in behind your ears. Damp fingertips on the sensors help.
Calibrate before you start — the app has no idea what focused looks like for you yet.
Your readings have drifted from the last calibration. Worth running it again.
Some permissions are missing, so notifications will be delivered normally.
Focused time by hour of day, across every session.
Turn the switch on from the Focus tab and the first session will show up here when it ends.
How long you have to be concentrating before the app starts holding notifications. Stops a momentary spike from silencing your phone.
A safety valve. Whatever the headset says, nothing is held back for longer than this.
Always on for now: the headset, signal and notification modules are not wired up yet, so everything runs on a synthetic signal.
Six-second blocks instead of sixty. Same nine blocks and the same phases, so the flow can be tested without sitting through it.
For offline analysis. Off by default — it writes a lot of data.
Skips calibration with untuned values so the rest of the app can be tested. Not fitted to you.
